label: r2c3
name: 2 epochs, longer credit horizon
hypothesis: Same network and 2-epoch recipe as r1c3, with gamma 0.99 and gae_lambda 0.95 instead of 0.95 and 0.9. Episodes run about 10 to 16 placements, so with gamma 0.95 the +1 for an exact build is heavily discounted at early steps. A longer horizon should give more credit to finishing exactly and less to stopping early. Refuted if dev success is no better than r1c3 (0.73) or if training becomes less stable.
last_analysis: Flipping the features along x (the mirror fix) is what made learning possible. Fewer PPO epochs, and so more samples, helped: r2c1 used 1 epoch and scored 0.86 on both seeds. r2c3 (2 epochs, gamma 0.99, lambda 0.95) is the best at 0.90. All three round-3 failures got stuck in the same way. Each has a seed scoring 0.078, mean IoU 0.714 and 0 cells placed outside the target. They build only layer 0, never stack, then choose DONE. This early trap is a matter of seed luck, not of capacity. The 1-epoch long-horizon run (r3c1) reached 0.83 on its other seed. The dilated conv cut the step count and gave no clear gain. So with only 3 trials left, I make small changes to r2c3 aimed at avoiding the ground-only trap. One gives more exploration, one gives credit over whole episodes instead of value bootstrapping, and one stops the critic from interfering with the DONE decision.
